<<<FILE environment/route.h>>>
#ifndef ROUTE_H
#define ROUTE_H

/*
 * SpeedyDeliver Route Library — Public API
 *
 * This library computes shortest routes in a directed graph with
 * non-negative integer edge weights (including zero).
 *
 * Tie-breaking rule
 * -----------------
 * Among equal-cost routes, the one whose node-id sequence is
 * lexicographically smallest is returned.  Comparison is element-by-
 * element from the source; a shorter sequence that is a prefix of a
 * longer one is considered smaller.
 *
 *   Example: path [0, 1, 3]  vs  path [0, 1, 2, 3]
 *     At position 2 the first has 3, the second has 2; 2 < 3,
 *     so [0, 1, 2, 3] is lexicographically smaller.
 *
 * Relaxation counter
 * ------------------
 * route_relaxations() returns the number of *distance-value*
 * comparisons performed during the most recent route_find() call.
 *
 * A distance-value comparison is any comparison where at least one
 * operand is a node's current shortest-path distance estimate.
 * Comparisons of node identifiers, array indices, or path arrays
 * for tie-breaking are NOT counted.
 *
 *   Examples of counted comparisons:
 *     - dist[i] < current_min   (scan in O(V²) Dijkstra)
 *     - dist[u] + w < dist[v]   (edge relaxation)
 *     - dist[u] + w == dist[v]  (equal-cost edge check)
 *     - heap-key comparisons where the key is a distance value
 *       (sift-up / sift-down in a binary-heap Dijkstra)
 *
 *   Examples of NOT counted comparisons:
 *     - node-id tie-breaking in the heap key
 *     - lexicographic path comparisons for tie-breaking
 *     - array-index bounds checks
 */

typedef struct RouteGraph RouteGraph;

/* Load a graph from a text file.
 * Format: first line "V E", then E lines "u v w".
 * Node ids are 0 .. V-1.  Weights are non-negative integers.
 * Returns NULL on error. */
RouteGraph* route_load(const char* filename);

/* Free a graph loaded by route_load. */
void route_free(RouteGraph* g);

/* Find the shortest path from src to dst.
 *
 * On success returns 0; *out_path is set to a malloc'd array of
 * node ids and *out_len to its length.  Caller must free *out_path.
 *
 * If dst is unreachable from src, returns -1 and sets *out_path to
 * NULL and *out_len to 0.
 *
 * Among equal-cost routes the lexicographically smallest node-id
 * sequence is returned (see above). */
int route_find(RouteGraph* g, int src, int dst,
               int** out_path, int* out_len);

/* Return the number of distance-value comparisons from the most
 * recent route_find() call (see definition above). */
long route_relaxations(void);

/* Return the total cost of the most recent successful route_find()
 * call.  Value is undefined after an unsuccessful call. */
long route_last_cost(void);

#endif /* ROUTE_H */
<<<END>>>
<<<FILE environment/route.c>>>
#include "route.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <limits.h>

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/*  Internal edge representation (singly-linked adjacency list)        */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

typedef struct Edge {
    int          to;
    long         weight;
    struct Edge* next;
} Edge;

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/*  RouteGraph definition                                             */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

struct RouteGraph {
    int    num_nodes;
    Edge** adj;          /* adj[u] -> linked list of edges from u       */
};

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/*  Module-level state for the counter / last-cost                     */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

static long g_relaxations = 0;
static long g_last_cost   = 0;

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/*  route_load                                                         */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

RouteGraph* route_load(const char* filename)
{
    FILE* f = fopen(filename, "r");
    if (!f) return NULL;

    int V, E;
    if (fscanf(f, "%d %d", &V, &E) != 2) { fclose(f); return NULL; }
    if (V < 0 || E < 0) { fclose(f); return NULL; }

    RouteGraph* g = (RouteGraph*)malloc(sizeof(RouteGraph));
    if (!g) { fclose(f); return NULL; }
    g->num_nodes = V;
    g->adj = (Edge**)calloc((size_t)V, sizeof(Edge*));
    if (!g->adj) { free(g); fclose(f); return NULL; }

    for (int i = 0; i < E; i++) {
        int u, v;
        long w;
        if (fscanf(f, "%d %d %ld", &u, &v, &w) != 3) break;
        if (u < 0 || u >= V || v < 0 || v >= V || w < 0) continue;

        Edge* e = (Edge*)malloc(sizeof(Edge));
        if (!e) break;
        e->to     = v;
        e->weight = w;
        e->next   = g->adj[u];
        g->adj[u] = e;
    }

    fclose(f);
    return g;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/*  route_free                                                         */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

void route_free(RouteGraph* g)
{
    if (!g) return;
    for (int i = 0; i < g->num_nodes; i++) {
        Edge* e = g->adj[i];
        while (e) {
            Edge* nxt = e->next;
            free(e);
            e = nxt;
        }
    }
    free(g->adj);
    free(g);
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/*  route_find  (STUB — to be implemented)                            */
/*                                                                     */
/*  The original O(V²) Dijkstra was removed for performance work.      */
/*  Replace this stub with a fast implementation that:                 */
/*    • uses a binary min-heap (or better) keyed by distance           */
/*    • among equal-cost routes returns the lexicographically smallest */
/*      node-id sequence  (see route.h for the full rule)              */
/*    • does NOT terminate early when dst is extracted — zero-weight   */
/*      edges from later-processed nodes can yield a lex-smaller       */
/*      equal-cost path                                                */
/*    • counts only distance-value comparisons (route.h)               */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

int route_find(RouteGraph* g, int src, int dst,
               int** out_path, int* out_len)
{
    (void)g; (void)src; (void)dst;
    g_relaxations = 0;
    g_last_cost   = 0;

    *out_path = NULL;
    *out_len  = 0;
    return -1;   /* always "unreachable" until implemented */
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/*  route_relaxations / route_last_cost                                */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

long route_relaxations(void) { return g_relaxations; }
long route_last_cost(void)   { return g_last_cost;   }
<<<END>>>
<<<FILE environment/main.c>>>
#include "route.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
    if (argc != 4) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Usage: %s GRAPH_FILE SRC DST\n", argv[0]);
        return 2;
    }

    RouteGraph* g = route_load(argv[1]);
    if (!g) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to load graph: %s\n", argv[1]);
        return 2;
    }

    int src = atoi(argv[2]);
    int dst = atoi(argv[3]);

    int* path    = NULL;
    int  path_len = 0;

    int result = route_find(g, src, dst, &path, &path_len);

    if (result != 0) {
        printf("unreachable\n");
        free(path);
        route_free(g);
        return 1;
    }

    for (int i = 0; i < path_len; i++) {
        if (i > 0) printf(" ");
        printf("%d", path[i]);
    }
    printf(" %ld\n", route_last_cost());

    free(path);
    route_free(g);
    return 0;
}

<<<FILE environment/Makefile>>>
CC      = gcc
CFLAGS  = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -std=c11
LDFLAGS =

route: main.o route.o
	$(CC) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ $^

main.o: main.c route.h
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<

route.o: route.c route.h
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<

clean:
	rm -f *.o route

.PHONY: clean

<<<FILE environment/README.md>>>
# SpeedyDeliver Route Library

A C library for computing shortest routes in directed graphs with
non-negative integer edge weights (including zero).

## Building

```sh
make
```

This produces the `route` executable.

## Usage

```sh
./route GRAPH_FILE SRC DST
```

- `GRAPH_FILE`: path to a graph text file
- `SRC`: source node id (integer, 0-based)
- `DST`: destination node id (integer, 0-based)

### Output

- **Reachable**: the node ids of the shortest route, space-separated,
  followed by a single space and the total cost as a decimal integer,
  followed by a newline.  Exit code 0.

  Example: `0 1 3 7` followed by a space, the cost, and a newline.

- **Unreachable**: the exact string `unreachable` followed by a newline.
  Exit code 1.

## Graph File Format

```
V E
u1 v1 w1
u2 v2 w2
...
```

- `V` — number of vertices (ids 0 … V−1)
- `E` — number of directed edges
- Each edge line: source `u`, target `v`, non-negative weight `w`

## C API

See `route.h` for full documentation.  Summary:

| Function | Description |
|---|---|
| `route_load(filename)` | Load a graph from file |
| `route_free(g)` | Free a loaded graph |
| `route_find(g, src, dst, &path, &len)` | Find shortest path; returns 0 on success, −1 if unreachable |
| `route_relaxations()` | Distance-value comparison count from last `route_find` |
| `route_last_cost()` | Total cost from last successful `route_find` |

## Tie-breaking

Among equal-cost routes, the one whose **node-id sequence is
lexicographically smallest** is returned.  See `route.h` for the
complete rule, including the prefix convention for paths of different
lengths.

## Relaxation counter

`route_relaxations()` counts **distance-value comparisons only** —
any comparison where at least one operand is a node's current
shortest-path distance estimate.  See `route.h` for the precise
definition and examples of what is and is not counted.

## Benchmark

Benchmark graphs and expected outputs live under `benchmark/`.

- `benchmark/graph_XX.txt` — graph files (seeds 0–4)
- `benchmark/expected/graph_XX.out` — expected output for each graph's queries
- `benchmark/baseline_relaxations.txt` — O(V²) relaxation counts per graph

## Running public tests

```sh
bash run_tests.sh
```

This checks output against the frozen expected files and verifies the
10× relaxation-count target on each benchmark graph.
<<<END>>>
<<<FILE environment/run_tests.sh>>>
#!/bin/bash
# Public test script — checks output against frozen expected files
# and verifies the 10× relaxation-count target.
set -euo pipefail

cd /app

echo "=== Building ==="
make clean >/dev/null 2>&1
make >/dev/null 2>&1

PASS=0
FAIL=0

check() {
    local label="$1"
    if [ "$2" = "0" ]; then
        PASS=$((PASS + 1))
    else
        FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
        echo "  FAIL: $label"
    fi
}

# ---- 1. Output correctness on benchmark graphs ----------------------

echo "=== Checking output against frozen expected files ==="

for gfile in benchmark/graph_*.txt; do
    name=$(basename "$gfile" .txt)
    expected="benchmark/expected/${name}.out"

    if [ ! -f "$expected" ]; then
        echo "  SKIP: no expected file for $name"
        continue
    fi

    # Read queries from expected file by replaying the same queries.
    # We store queries in a sidecar; if missing, skip.
    qfile="benchmark/${name}.queries"
    if [ ! -f "$qfile" ]; then
        echo "  SKIP: no query file for $name"
        continue
    fi

    actual_tmp=$(mktemp)
    while IFS=' ' read -r src dst; do
        ./route "$gfile" "$src" "$dst" >> "$actual_tmp" 2>/dev/null || true
    done < "$qfile"

    if diff -q "$actual_tmp" "$expected" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        check "$name output" 0
    else
        check "$name output" 1
        diff "$actual_tmp" "$expected" | head -5
    fi
    rm -f "$actual_tmp"
done

# ---- 2. Relaxation count ≤ baseline / 10 ----------------------------

echo "=== Checking relaxation counts ==="

if [ -f benchmark/baseline_relaxations.txt ]; then
    while IFS=' ' read -r name baseline; do
        gfile="benchmark/${name}.txt"
        qfile="benchmark/${name}.queries"

        if [ ! -f "$qfile" ]; then
            echo "  SKIP: no query file for $name"
            continue
        fi

        # Use first query for the relaxation-count check
        first_query=$(head -1 "$qfile")
        src=$(echo "$first_query" | cut -d' ' -f1)
        dst=$(echo "$first_query" | cut -d' ' -f2)

        # Run route; capture exit code
        set +e
        output=$(./route "$gfile" "$src" "$dst" 2>&1)
        rc=$?
        set -e

        # We need route_relaxations — call a tiny helper if the binary
        # supports it.  Since the CLI does not expose the counter,
        # we compile a small test program.
        cat > /tmp/test_relax.c <<'CEOF'
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include "route.h"
int main(int argc, char** argv) {
    if (argc < 4) return 2;
    RouteGraph* g = route_load(argv[1]);
    if (!g) return 2;
    int src = atoi(argv[2]), dst = atoi(argv[3]);
    int* path = NULL; int plen = 0;
    route_find(g, src, dst, &path, &plen);
    printf("%ld\n", route_relaxations());
    free(path);
    route_free(g);
    return 0;
}
CEOF
        gcc -O2 -o /tmp/test_relax /tmp/test_relax.c route.o -I. 2>/dev/null
        if [ -x /tmp/test_relax ]; then
            agent_count=$(/tmp/test_relax "$gfile" "$src" "$dst" 2>/dev/null || echo "999999999")
        else
            agent_count="999999999"
        fi

        threshold=$((baseline / 10))
        if [ "$threshold" -le 0 ]; then threshold=1; fi
        if [ "$agent_count" -le "$threshold" ]; then
            check "$name relaxations ($agent_count <= $threshold)" 0
        else
            check "$name relaxations ($agent_count > $threshold)" 1
        fi
    done < benchmark/baseline_relaxations.txt
fi

# ---- Summary --------------------------------------------------------

echo ""
echo "=== Results: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed ==="
if [ "$FAIL" -gt 0 ]; then
    exit 1
fi
exit 0
<<<END>>>
<<<FILE environment/scripts/gen_benchmark.py>>>
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate benchmark graphs for the SpeedyDeliver route library.

Creates 5 directed graphs (seeds 0–4) under the given output directory,
plus a queries file listing src–dst pairs for each graph.
"""

import os
import random
import sys


def write_graph(path, V, edges):
    with open(path, "w") as f:
        f.write(f"{V} {len(edges)}\n")
        for u, v, w in edges:
            f.write(f"{u} {v} {w}\n")


def gen_sparse_random(rng, V, e_factor=3, zero_prob=0.0, wmax=10):
    """Sparse random directed graph; guaranteed weakly connected."""
    E_target = V * e_factor
    edges = []
    seen = set()

    def _add(u, v, w):
        if (u, v) not in seen and u != v:
            seen.add((u, v))
            edges.append((u, v, w))
            return True
        return False

    # spanning tree for connectivity
    order = list(range(V))
    rng.shuffle(order)
    for i in range(1, V):
        parent = order[rng.randint(0, i - 1)]
        child = order[i]
        w = 0 if rng.random() < zero_prob else rng.randint(1, wmax)
        _add(parent, child, w)
        # add reverse to make it strongly connected
        rw = 0 if rng.random() < zero_prob else rng.randint(1, wmax)
        _add(child, parent, rw)

    # extra random edges
    tries = 0
    while len(edges) < E_target and tries < E_target * 20:
        u = rng.randint(0, V - 1)
        v = rng.randint(0, V - 1)
        w = 0 if rng.random() < zero_prob else rng.randint(1, wmax)
        _add(u, v, w)
        tries += 1

    return V, edges


def gen_grid(rng, rows, cols, wrange=(1, 1)):
    """Bidirectional grid graph."""
    V = rows * cols
    edges = []
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            n = r * cols + c
            if c + 1 < cols:
                w = rng.randint(wrange[0], wrange[1])
                edges.append((n, n + 1, w))
                edges.append((n + 1, n, w))
            if r + 1 < rows:
                w = rng.randint(wrange[0], wrange[1])
                edges.append((n, n + cols, w))
                edges.append((n + cols, n, w))
    return V, edges


def gen_disconnected(rng, specs):
    """Multiple disconnected components."""
    all_edges = []
    offset = 0
    comp_ranges = []
    for cV, cseed, cef in specs:
        crng = random.Random(cseed)
        V, edges = gen_sparse_random(crng, cV, e_factor=cef)
        all_edges.extend((u + offset, v + offset, w) for u, v, w in edges)
        comp_ranges.append((offset, offset + cV))
        offset += cV
    return offset, all_edges, comp_ranges


def main():
    out = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "."
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(out, "expected"), exist_ok=True)

    graphs = {}  # name -> (V, edges, queries)

    # graph_00 — sparse random, ~200 nodes
    V0, E0 = gen_sparse_random(random.Random(0), 200, e_factor=3)
    graphs["graph_00"] = (V0, E0, [(0, 199), (0, 100), (50, 150)])

    # graph_01 — sparse random, ~350 nodes
    V1, E1 = gen_sparse_random(random.Random(1), 350, e_factor=3)
    graphs["graph_01"] = (V1, E1, [(0, 349), (0, 175), (100, 250)])

    # graph_02 — 20×20 grid, unit weights  →  many equal-cost routes
    V2, E2 = gen_grid(random.Random(2), 20, 20, wrange=(1, 1))
    graphs["graph_02"] = (V2, E2, [(0, 399), (0, 209), (10, 389)])

    # graph_03 — sparse random with zero-weight edges, ~400 nodes
    V3, E3 = gen_sparse_random(random.Random(3), 400, e_factor=3,
                               zero_prob=0.15)
    graphs["graph_03"] = (V3, E3, [(0, 399), (0, 200), (100, 300)])

    # graph_04 — disconnected (3 components)
    V4, E4, cr = gen_disconnected(random.Random(4), [
        (300, 40, 3),
        (150, 41, 3),
        (150, 42, 3),
    ])
    graphs["graph_04"] = (V4, E4, [
        (0, 299),       # reachable  (component 1)
        (0, 300),       # unreachable (comp1 → comp2)
        (300, 449),     # reachable  (component 2)
        (450, 599),     # reachable  (component 3)
    ])

    # write graph files
    for name, (V, edges, _) in graphs.items():
        write_graph(os.path.join(out, f"{name}.txt"), V, edges)

    # write per-graph query files
    for name, (_, _, queries) in graphs.items():
        with open(os.path.join(out, f"{name}.queries"), "w") as f:
            for s, d in queries:
                f.write(f"{s} {d}\n")

    # write master queries list (for the generate.sh script)
    with open(os.path.join(out, "queries.txt"), "w") as f:
        for name, (_, _, queries) in graphs.items():
            for s, d in queries:
                f.write(f"{name} {s} {d}\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
<<<END>>>
<<<FILE environment/scripts/ref_route.c>>`
/* ref_route.c — Reference implementation used ONLY at build time
 *               to produce frozen expected outputs and baseline
 *               relaxation counts.
 *
 * Algorithm:
 *   1. O(V²) forward Dijkstra from src  (distance comparisons counted)
 *   2. O(V²) reverse Dijkstra from dst  (not counted — tie-breaking only)
 *   3. Greedy DFS on the shortest-path DAG for the lex-smallest path
 *
 * This file is deleted from the image after benchmark generation.
 */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <limits.h>

/* ---------- graph structures ---------------------------------------- */

typedef struct RefEdge {
    int          to;
    long         weight;
    struct RefEdge* next;
} RefEdge;

typedef struct {
    int       V;
    RefEdge** adj;     /* forward adjacency */
    RefEdge** radj;    /* reverse adjacency  */
} RefGraph;

/* ---------- load / free -------------------------------------------- */

static RefGraph* ref_load(const char* fn)
{
    FILE* f = fopen(fn, "r");
    if (!f) return NULL;
    int V, E;
    if (fscanf(f, "%d %d", &V, &E) != 2) { fclose(f); return NULL; }
    RefGraph* g = (RefGraph*)calloc(1, sizeof(RefGraph));
    g->V    = V;
    g->adj  = (RefEdge**)calloc(V, sizeof(RefEdge*));
    g->radj = (RefEdge**)calloc(V, sizeof(RefEdge*));
    for (int i = 0; i < E; i++) {
        int u, v; long w;
        if (fscanf(f, "%d %d %ld", &u, &v, &w) != 3) break;
        RefEdge* e1 = (RefEdge*)malloc(sizeof(RefEdge));
        e1->to = v; e1->weight = w; e1->next = g->adj[u]; g->adj[u] = e1;
        RefEdge* e2 = (RefEdge*)malloc(sizeof(RefEdge));
        e2->to = u; e2->weight = w; e2->next = g->radj[v]; g->radj[v] = e2;
    }
    fclose(f);
    return g;
}

static void ref_free(RefGraph* g)
{
    if (!g) return;
    for (int i = 0; i < g->V; i++) {
        for (RefEdge* e = g->adj[i]; e; )  { RefEdge* n = e->next; free(e); e = n; }
        for (RefEdge* e = g->radj[i]; e; ) { RefEdge* n = e->next; free(e); e = n; }
    }
    free(g->adj); free(g->radj); free(g);
}

/* ---------- O(V²) Dijkstra ----------------------------------------- */

static void dijkstra_v2(RefEdge** adj, int V, int src,
                        long* dist, long* relax_count)
{
    int* vis = (int*)calloc(V, sizeof(int));
    *relax_count = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < V; i++) dist[i] = LONG_MAX;
    dist[src] = 0;

    for (int iter = 0; iter < V; iter++) {
        int  u  = -1;
        long md = LONG_MAX;
        /* Scan ALL V nodes — dist[i] < md is always a distance comparison
         * (even for visited nodes).  This matches the baseline counting. */
        for (int i = 0; i < V; i++) {
            (*relax_count)++;                    /* dist[i] < md  */
            if (dist[i] < md && !vis[i]) {
                md = dist[i];
                u  = i;
            }
        }
        if (u == -1 || md == LONG_MAX) break;
        vis[u] = 1;

        for (RefEdge* e = adj[u]; e; e = e->next) {
            long nd = dist[u] + e->weight;
            (*relax_count)++;                    /* nd < dist[v]  */
            if (nd < dist[e->to]) {
                dist[e->to] = nd;
            }
            /* We do NOT count the == check here because the original
             * O(V²) baseline only counted < comparisons for edges.
             * Tie-breaking is handled separately (steps 2-3). */
        }
    }
    free(vis);
}

/* ---------- Lex-smallest path via greedy DFS ----------------------- */

/* Iterative DFS that always picks the smallest-id next node on a
 * shortest path.  Backtracks on dead-ends (zero-weight cycles).
 * Returns path length, or -1 on failure. */

static int lex_path(RefGraph* g, long* dist, long* rdist,
                    long target, int src, int dst,
                    int* out_path)
{
    int* on_path = (int*)calloc(g->V, sizeof(int));
    /* stack of (node, next_edge_to_try) */
    typedef struct { int node; RefEdge* edge; } Frame;
    Frame* stk = (Frame*)malloc((size_t)g->V * 2 * sizeof(Frame));
    int    top = 0;
    int    plen = 0;

    out_path[plen++] = src;
    on_path[src] = 1;
    stk[top].node = src;
    stk[top].edge = g->adj[src];
    top++;

    while (top > 0) {
        int cur = stk[top - 1].node;
        if (cur == dst) break;          /* found */

        /* Find smallest-id unvisited next node on a shortest path */
        int best = -1;
        RefEdge* best_edge = NULL;
        RefEdge* start = stk[top - 1].edge;
        for (RefEdge* e = start; e; e = e->next) {
            int v = e->to;
            if (!on_path[v] &&
                rdist[v] != LONG_MAX &&
                dist[cur] + e->weight + rdist[v] == target)
            {
                if (best == -1 || v < best) {
                    best = v;
                    best_edge = e;
                }
            }
        }

        if (best == -1) {
            /* dead end — backtrack */
            top--;
            on_path[cur] = 0;
            plen--;
            continue;
        }

        /* Advance past the edge we're about to take, so on backtrack
         * we try edges after it.  We record the edge AFTER best_edge
         * as the resume point. */
        /* Find the edge after best_edge in the list starting from
         * stk[top-1].edge, so that backtracking can resume correctly.
         * Simpler approach: on backtrack, re-scan from the next edge
         * after best_edge. */
        RefEdge* resume = stk[top - 1].edge;
        /* skip up to and including best_edge */
        while (resume && resume != best_edge) resume = resume->next;
        if (resume) resume = resume->next;
        stk[top - 1].edge = resume;     /* update resume point */

        /* Push new node if we haven't exhausted this level yet */
        if (best != -1) {
            on_path[best] = 1;
            out_path[plen++] = best;
            stk[top].node = best;
            stk[top].edge = g->adj[best];
            top++;
        }
    }

    free(stk);
    free(on_path);

    if (top > 0 && out_path[plen - 1] == dst)
        return plen;
    return -1;
}

/* ---------- main --------------------------------------------------- */

int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
    if (argc < 4) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Usage: ref_route GRAPH SRC DST\n");
        return 2;
    }
    RefGraph* g = ref_load(argv[1]);
    if (!g) { fprintf(stderr, "load failed\n"); return 2; }
    int src = atoi(argv[2]);
    int dst = atoi(argv[3]);

    /* 1. Forward Dijkstra */
    long* dist = (long*)malloc(g->V * sizeof(long));
    long  fwd_relax;
    dijkstra_v2(g->adj, g->V, src, dist, &fwd_relax);

    if (dist[dst] == LONG_MAX) {
        printf("unreachable\n");
        fprintf(stderr, "%ld\n", fwd_relax);
        ref_free(g); free(dist);
        return 1;
    }

    /* 2. Reverse Dijkstra from dst */
    long* rdist = (long*)malloc(g->V * sizeof(long));
    long  rev_relax;
    dijkstra_v2(g->radj, g->V, dst, rdist, &rev_relax);

    /* 3. Lex-smallest path via DFS */
    long target = dist[dst];
    int* path = (int*)malloc(g->V * sizeof(int));
    int  plen = lex_path(g, dist, rdist, target, src, dst, path);

    if (plen < 0) {
        /* should not happen if dst is reachable */
        printf("unreachable\n");
        fprintf(stderr, "%ld\n", fwd_relax);
        ref_free(g); free(dist); free(rdist); free(path);
        return 1;
    }

    for (int i = 0; i < plen; i++) {
        if (i > 0) printf(" ");
        printf("%d", path[i]);
    }
    printf(" %ld\n", dist[dst]);

    /* relaxation count to stderr */
    fprintf(stderr, "%ld\n", fwd_relax);

    ref_free(g); free(dist); free(rdist); free(path);
    return 0;
}
<<<END>>>
<<<FILE environment/scripts/generate.sh>>>
#!/bin/bash
# Run at Docker build time to create benchmark data.
# Deletes itself and the reference implementation afterwards.
set -euo pipefail

cd /app

echo ">>> Generating benchmark graphs"
python3 scripts/gen_benchmark.py benchmark

echo ">>> Compiling reference implementation"
gcc -O2 -o ref_route scripts/ref_route.c -lm

echo ">>> Running reference to produce expected outputs"
mkdir -p benchmark/expected
> benchmark/baseline_relaxations.txt

prev_graph=""
while IFS=' ' read -r graph_name src dst; do
    graph_file="benchmark/${graph_name}.txt"
    expected_file="benchmark/expected/${graph_name}.out"

    # Run reference; stdout → path output, stderr → relax count
    path_out=$(./ref_route "$graph_file" "$src" "$dst" 2>/tmp/ref_err) || true
    relax=$(cat /tmp/ref_err)

    # Append to per-graph expected file
    echo "$path_out" >> "$expected_file"

    # Record baseline relaxation count for the first query of each graph
    if [ "$graph_name" != "$prev_graph" ]; then
        echo "${graph_name} ${relax}" >> benchmark/baseline_relaxations.txt
        prev_graph="$graph_name"
    fi
done < benchmark/queries.txt

echo ">>> Baseline relaxation counts:"
cat benchmark/baseline_relaxations.txt

echo ">>> Cleaning up reference and generator"
rm -f ref_route /tmp/ref_err
rm -f scripts/ref_route.c scripts/gen_benchmark.py scripts/generate.sh
rm -f benchmark/queries.txt

echo ">>> Benchmark generation complete"
<<<END>>>
